decisions.why: Bookkeeping of the ranking's history; it moves no open row and changes no fix.

decisions.summary: Wave 6 is the 32 open E0 rows (tasks.md Phase 7), claim lines only

decisions.summary: No map regeneration, review occasion or perf bookend for wave 6
decisions.why: Claim lines change nothing a map draws; FR-005's regeneration and occasions apply to waves that change drawing, and the bookend rule to waves that change engine behavior.

decisions.summary: A claim written or relabeled never carries a code change; where the page it names answers differently from the code, the claim states the code against that page and the departure is ranked as a found row in its own tier
decisions.why: The rewording only extends the rule from relabels to claims written for UNCLAIMED units, which is the same case (Phase 7 is both). The code still moves to the research (FR-004), in the tier its work takes (FR-003, Edge Cases 'new findings a fix exposes'); the claim stays a drift, not a DEVIATION (T22 allows DEVIATION only via the exception path), so the departure stays a finding until fixed. Nothing is dropped; it is ordered, as the GM asked.

decisions.summary: Later waves take their regression baseline on the clone while its engine content is main's, before the wave's first edit
decisions.why: A verification method under constitution XIII; it does not touch the scope of what the GM asked.

decisions.summary: Scope from the kept maps' own gen-cache entries only (KEPT_MAPS: pool hamlets, magistracy sheets, country shrine; never .gencache/rolls, h10, h20): a recorded function or method, a class one of whose methods ran, a constant an executed function reads BY NAME, any unit under hamletgen/, KEPT_CHECKS, buildings* as mode-a; everything else deferred (924 of 3945)
decisions.why: Round 2's items answered and reproduced on round 3's own run (scope.json and claims-deferred.json identical; 271/60/162; the kept maps' entries dated 2026-10-07 09:17-09:25; today's current-code Inashiro HamletSpec roll adds 0 functions; hamletgen/ is imported by no legacy path but finish.py's strip_reaches_view). But the measure cannot see code the scripted hamlets execute through the knob registry or at a module's top level, so it marks their findings DEFERRED, against 'limit ourselves to code actually executed by ... scripted hamlets; legacy hand-drawn settlements shall have their findings marked as DEFERRED'. Measured: grain.py::WINTER_CROP (row 456, E2) is resolved by name (resolve_knob('winter_crop')) in CombMixin._coarse_grain_top_up, which all five pool hamlets' records hold; _knobs.py::<module>#kosatsuba_seat forms (row 633, E3) is the knob board_seat.py resolves, whose typing rule _kosatsuba_seat_ok is in all five hamlets' records - scope_of defers every <module> claim unconditionally; paddy.py::PADDY_REST and bridges.py::FOOTBRIDGE_FORM sit on the deferred list though resting_plots and channel_footbridges (all five records) resolve them. 20 classes executed code names (e.g. land/tiles.py::Cover, structures/fixtures/board_seat.py BoardSeat and SiteEnv, rolling/bundle.py::PocketUnlaid) are deferred because no Python-level method ran. Not impossible (the knob name and the typing rule are both measurable), and nothing in the request implies deferring hamlet code. Wave 9's rows are unaffected (456 and 633 are E2/E3; row 275 FixtureForms#privy seat weights stays deferred on substance: fixture_forms overrides the default, which only bundle.py:444's fallback reads).
